sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year, from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
FY2019 was the one break in the window: operating income fell to $5.5 billion from $13.4 billion in FY2018 and operating margin dropped 11.9pp to 8.1% [F13][F12][D109][F23].
The filings tie FY2019 to a $6.8 billion Shave Care goodwill impairment, attributed to currency devaluations, slower category growth and heavier competition [X109][P62].
FY2020 operating income then rose 186.2% to $15.7 billion, largely because the FY2019 impairment charge dropped out of the base [D148][F14][P71].
The US drove the window: US revenue reached $41.7 billion in FY2026 against $27.3 billion in FY2018, lifting its share of revenue from 40.8% to 47.9% [S18][S10][D512][D534].
In FY2026 the mix flipped: Non-US contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth and the US only 0.1pp [D511][D536][D457].
Management attributes FY2026 net sales growth to favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26][D457].
Beauty grew 7.1% and added 1.3pp, ahead of Fabric & Home Care, the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue, which added 0.8pp [D602][D603][D541][D543].
Operating leverage was negative in FY2026, with operating income down 3.4% on revenue up 3.3% and an incremental margin of -25.6% [D458][D457][D481].
Over the window, diluted shares fell from 2,740.4 million to 2,422.5 million, so diluted EPS compounded at 1.9% against net income at 0.5% [X115][X124][F205][F203].
Operating margin of 22.7% in FY2026 sits above the window median of 22.1% but below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [F30][D648][D647].
Against 5 staples peers it ranks at the 80th percentile, with the peer median at 14.3% [D668][D669].
The 1.6pp FY2026 decline came from cost of revenue (-1.0pp) and SG&A (-0.6pp), which the filing ascribes to lower gross margin and higher marketing spending [D470][D483][D485][P25].
The FY2019 residual of -12.1pp corresponds to the goodwill impairment recorded that year [D125][X109][P62].

Net income still rose 0.5% in FY2026 because other non-operating income reached $1.1 billion from $154 million, helped by the Glad joint venture dissolution gain and the absence of the prior-year Argentina charge [X108][X107][D459][P24].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, but free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, below the window median of 1.02x [F80][D444][F100][D445][D660].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is close to the 17.2% window median [D441][D654].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, or 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A [D464][F90][D440][D446]; the filings cited do not explain the step-up.
Inventory build consumed $641 million in FY2026, driven by higher safety stock and new product initiatives, while payables supplied $919 million [P3].
Net debt was $24.2 billion in FY2026, down from $24.9 billion, or 27.8% of revenue [D450][D399][D451].
That is the 33rd percentile among 6 staples peers on net cash to revenue, with a peer median of -1.0% [D676][D677].
Return on average equity of 30.1% is also at the 33rd percentile, against a peer median of 44.4% [D456][D680][D681].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion and dividends of $10.2 billion totalled $15.3 billion, or 100.7% of free cash flow [X134][X144][D452][D453].
Diluted shares fell 1.3% in FY2026, while acquisitions were only $85 million [D476][X154].
Current ratio was 0.68x in FY2026, below 1.0x, with working capital of -$12.5 billion [F180][F170][R1].
It was below 1.0x in every year of the window, with a high of 0.88x, so it looks structural, but $6.5 billion of current debt maturities leave refinancing exposure [D662][X194].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453][R2].
Returns that exceed free cash flow can only be sustained with debt or cash, and net debt has barely fallen [D453][D450][D399].
Days inventory reached 69 in FY2026 from 52 in FY2017, with inventory up 8.2% against revenue up 3.3% [D455][D21][D480][D457].
Management cites safety stock and new products [P3], but with unit volume flat [P26] the build ties up cash without volume support.

Operating margin holding above the 22.1% window median would confirm stabilisation from the FY2026 level of 22.7%, and a fall below it would reverse that view [D648][F30]; the test is the FY2027 10-K.
Buybacks plus dividends staying above the FY2026 level of 100.7% of free cash flow would confirm the funding strain [D453]; the test is the FY2027 10-K.
Capex staying above 5.1% of revenue while free cash flow margin stays below the 17.4% reported in FY2026 would confirm falling conversion [D440][D441]; the test is the FY2027 10-K.
Days inventory rising above 69 days would confirm the working-capital drag [D455]; the test is the FY2027 10-K.
